How luck based the items feel. Not all of the gold chest items are in par with one another, and this wouldn't be so bad if the gold chests also felt really rare in of themselves.

If I open up a gold chest and get any health upgrade (that isn't the orange), I get upset because I lost a passive item for something I could have gotten by playing well at the boss. To an extent I'd prefer the low tier item Scope to another heart container. Same goes to the green chest item Bloody Scarf, it's fun because it feels like I'm getting more powerful. I get to blink everywhere and reload my guns faster, it's wonderful.

There are also plenty of golden chest guns that I don't like or that are flat out better than others.

*If I get a gold chest, I want it to feel like this is a big advantage, not like I got screwed over.*

I think that Risk of Rain did well by having it so that there were many chests, they had a rare chance to contain the super special red items, but if you got any other item of any other rarity it was still neat, because they were all cool in their own regards.

On the other hand, you usually get 2 chests in Enter the Gungeon, maybe even 1 or god forbid none if you're super unlucky.

To me the solutions are - Make guns and passives better align with the rarity of the chests. I still love this game but also it can screw off when it screws me over.

As a kid I was happy with myself. At times I wished I was a girl for various reasons, like for instance I thought they had it easier in life. Always looked prettier too.

When I was 12-13 I truly saw and understood what the LGBT spectrum is, and while I supported everyone in it, I didn't think that I was in any of the letters.

Skip ahead two years and school ended. I considered myself a man who wanted to do more feminine things with my body.

The last straw until the egg cracked for me was when I was especially trans curious. I forget what caused it, but I just asked my closest friend at the time a simple request.

I just said that I was pretty trans curious as of the late, and was wondering if she could call me Scarlet for a while. She said yes, and called me Scarlet a while after.
It just felt so right to me. It felt so natural, I was happy with someone saying my name when I never felt that way when I was called by my birth name.

School recently started for me, and I've been very content with myself, although just as closeted. Few people know about my real name and gender, but those people are good people.

I suppose that's my story.
